plotting_plan.title: Topic-Bottleneck Query Reformulation Pipeline
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Block Diagram) of the six-step pipeline: topic extraction, S0 text generation, optional vocabulary exclusion, proxy question generation, question selection, cloud answering, and local synthesis. Show data flow boundaries (local vs. cloud) and sensitivity levels at each stage.

plotting_plan.title: Specific Value Recovery Rate: Topic Bottleneck vs. DP Sanitization
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Bar Chart) comparing specific value recovery rates: our pipeline (2.3%) vs. DP-sanitized text attacked by LLaMA-2 70B (72.18%), LLaMA-3 70B (82.39%), Gemma-2 (75.35%), GPT-4o (91.2%), Claude-3.5 Sonnet (94.01%). Include a dashed red line at 10% threshold.

plotting_plan.title: Performance by Task Type
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Heatmap) showing BERTScore F1, semantic similarity, gold span overlap, and specific value recovery across four task types (framework/reasoning, compliance/regulatory, procedural, entity-specific). Highlights the operating envelope boundary.

plotting_plan.title: Quality vs. Privacy Trade-off Across Methods
plotting_plan.objective: Visual summary (Scatter Plot) with x-axis = specific value recovery rate (privacy, lower is better) and y-axis = BERTScore F1 (quality, higher is better). Plot points for: our pipeline (2.3%, 0.893), our pipeline + vocab exclusion (0%, 0.823), entity substitution baseline (estimated from literature), DP methods (91-94% recovery, varying quality). Show Pareto frontier.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: State-of-the-art LLMs are cloud-only, creating a fundamental tension for enterprises with classified data: LLM value scales with prompt specificity, but privacy requires removing specificity before transmission.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Existing privacy-preserving approaches (entity substitution, differential privacy) are fundamentally reversible -- modern LLMs recover 72-94% of original sensitive content from DP-sanitized text. No existing method provides an irreversible information bottleneck that structurally prevents reconstruction.
search_directions: Find foundational papers on differential privacy for text (SanText, CusText, TEM) and their empirical privacy guarantees
Search for LLM-based reconstruction attacks on DP-sanitized text, especially arXiv:2410.12443 demonstrating 91-94% recovery rates
Identify enterprise privacy-preserving LLM inference frameworks (Presidio, PRISM, CON-QA, HaS) and their limitations
Search for information bottleneck theory applied to privacy, including topic modeling as a compression mechanism
Find papers on privacy-preserving QA in legal/contract domains (CUAD dataset, CON-QA) as evaluation baselines
Identify surveys on text anonymization metrics and their alignment with GDPR/HIPAA requirements

related_work_strategy.overview: Investigate three specific paradigms that represent the landscape of privacy-preserving LLM inference, establishing that each has a fundamental reversibility limitation that the topic-bottleneck approach resolves.

subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify current SOTA entity substitution methods (Presidio, HaS, CON-QA, Anonymous-by-Construction, RUPTA, LLM-Redactor) and their privacy guarantees. Determine whether any achieves provable resistance to LLM-based re-identification attacks.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Entity substitution creates a one-to-one mapping between original and pseudonymized entities, which is structurally invertible by modern LLMs that can reason over dispersed contextual patterns.
limitation_search_queries: LLM re-identification attacks on pseudonymized text
Entity substitution reversibility in privacy-preserving NLP
Contextual re-identification beyond named entity recognition
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our topic-bottleneck approach avoids entity-level substitution entirely by compressing through a many-to-one semantic bottleneck, making reconstruction structurally impossible rather than merely statistically difficult.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Token-level DP perturbation and embedding noise
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify the strongest DP text sanitization methods (SanText, CusText, TEM, CAPE, InferDPT, DYNTEXT, CluSanT) and their best-case privacy-utility trade-offs. Critically, establish the reconstruction attack results from Pang et al. (arXiv:2410.12443) showing 91-94% recovery.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Token-level DP noise is reversible because modern LLMs memorize broad training data distributions and can bridge sanitized-to-original mappings via in-context learning, achieving 72-94% recovery rates.
limitation_search_queries: Reconstruction attacks on differentially private text sanitization
LLM memorization and differential privacy circumvention
Privacy-utility Pareto frontier for text DP methods
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Unlike DP methods that perturb the original text (leaving recoverable traces), our pipeline never transmits a modified version of the sensitive text -- it transmits independently generated S0 proxy questions derived from topic distributions, with no bijective mapping to the original.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.3 Hybrid Cloud-Edge and Split Inference Approaches
subsections.methodology_cluster: Architectural partitioning of inference across trust boundaries
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify cloud-edge routing (PRISM), split inference (SnD, speculative decoding), TEE-based (Confidential LLM, GELO), and FHE/MPC approaches (EncryptedLLM, PermLLM). Assess their deployment readiness and privacy guarantees.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Hardware-based approaches (TEE, FHE) provide strong guarantees but require specialized infrastructure. Software-based split inference leaks information through intermediate activations. No approach achieves both strong privacy and immediate deployability with commodity hardware.
limitation_search_queries: Privacy leakage from split LLM inference intermediate activations
TEE overhead for LLM inference deployment cost
Practical deployment barriers for FHE and MPC in LLM inference
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our approach requires only a local SLM and cloud API access -- no specialized hardware, no model modifications, no cryptographic protocols. It achieves privacy through information-theoretic compression rather than computational hardness assumptions.

subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Identify data minimization approaches (Zhou et al. showing GPT-4 tolerates 85.7% redaction), privacy-preserving RAG (synthetic data substitution, DP-RAG), and the privacy metrics survey (arXiv:2512.01109) showing no metric maps to legal compliance.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Data minimization reduces information quantity but does not guarantee that remaining information is non-sensitive. RAG privacy focuses on corpus protection, not prompt privacy. No existing framework addresses semantic-level sensitivity classification with graduated sanitization.
limitation_search_queries: Data minimization for LLM prompts empirical evaluation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our pipeline operationalizes data minimization at the semantic level: the topic bottleneck transmits only the minimum information needed (topic structure) while ensuring that all sensitive specifics are irreversibly compressed away.

content_bullets: Contribution 1: Topic modeling as an irreversible information bottleneck for privacy. Many-to-one compression makes reconstruction structurally impossible.
Contribution 2: Vocabulary exclusion as a novel hardening layer that strips domain vocabulary from generated text, not found in existing literature.
Contribution 3: Local synthesis architecture where the local LLM applies cloud-obtained S0 reasoning frameworks to locally-held S2 specifics.
Contribution 4: Empirical operating envelope characterization by task type on CUAD dataset: 2.3% specific value recovery vs. 91-94% for DP methods, with 89.3% BERTScore F1 quality preservation.

Survey entity substitution methods: Presidio-style NER replacement, HaS two-stage anonymize-and-recover, CON-QA one-to-many anonymization, Anonymous-by-Construction, RUPTA with LLM re-identification defense, LLM-Redactor eight-technique benchmark.
Highlight that all methods maintain a bijective or near-bijective mapping between original and sanitized text, making them vulnerable to LLM-based contextual re-identification.

subsections.subsection_title: 4.2 Topic Extraction and S0 Text Generation
content_bullets: Detail Steps 1-2: local LLM extracts topic distribution from S2 question, then generates 200-300 words of generic S0 text about those topics. Explain the many-to-one compression property: an enormous number of different S2 prompts map to the same topic distribution.
Formalize the information bottleneck: the topic distribution is a lossy compression that preserves reasoning structure while stripping sensitive specifics.
citation_hints: research paper or technical report introducing 'information bottleneck method'
research paper or technical report introducing 'Latent Dirichlet Allocation'

content_bullets: Detail Step 2.5: strip all topic-vocabulary words from the generated S0 text before question generation. Explain as a second layer of many-to-one compression.

Present the absence fingerprint vulnerability: attacker who infers the topic can diff expected vs. observed vocabulary. Describe the four proposed mitigations from idea.md: random over-exclusion, paraphrase replacement, generation-time avoidance (recommended), fixed-size vocabulary masking.
Present this as a composable hardening layer for S3 data, not the default configuration.

Detail Steps 3-4: generate 10 candidate S0 proxy questions from the (optionally vocabulary-stripped) text, then select the 3 most relevant by comparing against the original S2 question using the local LLM.
Emphasize that the original S2 question is seen only by the local LLM in Step 4 -- it never leaves the local environment.
Detail Steps 5-6: send 3 S0 proxy questions to cloud LLM, receive S0 answers. Local LLM combines original S2 question with the 3 cloud-obtained S0 answers to produce final answer.
Draw the consultant analogy from idea.md: look up best practices externally, apply them to a confidential internal situation.
CUAD (Contract Understanding Atticus Dataset) dev split, 48 answerable legal contract QA pairs. Cite CUAD.
Four task types with 12 samples each: framework/reasoning, compliance/regulatory, procedural, entity-specific. Explain task type assignment rationale.

content_bullets: Report headline result: 2.3% mean specific value recovery rate across both attack variants. Compare with 91-94% for DP methods (arXiv:2410.12443). Reference Figure fig_recovery_rate_comparison.
Break down by attack variant: direct recovery prompt (2.1%), domain expert prompt (2.5%). Domain recovery is high (90-94%) but accepted as intentional.
Report vocabulary exclusion ablation: 0% specific value recovery with vocab exclusion enabled. Reference Figure fig_quality_privacy_scatter.
citation_hints: Shuchao Pang et al. (Reconstruction of Differentially Private Text Sanitization via LLMs)

content_bullets: Report pipeline quality: 89.3% BERTScore F1, 85.3% semantic similarity, 22.5% gold span overlap vs. oracle.
Compare with baselines: local-only (93.3% BERTScore but no cloud reasoning), entity substitution (82.0% BERTScore, 58.1% semantic similarity).
Report vocabulary exclusion quality cost: BERTScore drops from 89.3% to 82.3% (-7.0%), semantic similarity drops from 85.3% to 41.3% (-44.0%).
Interpret: pipeline produces longer reasoning-based answers (1.61x oracle length) rather than extracting text spans.
Present per-task-type results with confidence intervals from experimental_log.md. Reference Figure fig_task_type_heatmap.
Framework/reasoning, compliance, procedural: zero specific value recovery with BERTScore 0.886-0.890.
Entity-specific: 9.2% specific value recovery, 0.65 gold span overlap. Note RUBIOSRESTAURANTSINC outlier with 100% recovery on a document name query.
Confirm the operating envelope hypothesis from idea.md: strong for reasoning/compliance/procedural, weak for entity-specific.

Explain the structural argument: topic modeling is many-to-one compression. DP noise is many-to-many perturbation within a recoverable neighborhood. Entity substitution is one-to-one mapping. Only many-to-one compression is irreversible.
Connect to the empirical result: 2.3% recovery vs. 91-94% is not an incremental improvement -- it is a qualitative difference in the privacy mechanism.

Formalize the operating envelope: the pipeline handles 60-70% of enterprise LLM use cases (reasoning, compliance, process) with strong privacy. Quantitative/entity-specific queries should be routed to local models or TEE-based inference.
Present the graduated deployment model from 06_proposed_pipeline.md: S1 data -> standard bottleneck; S2 -> bottleneck + vocab exclusion consideration; S3 -> bottleneck + vocab exclusion mandatory.
Discuss the vocabulary exclusion trade-off: perfect privacy (0% recovery) but steep quality cost (semantic similarity drops 44%). Recommend as optional hardening for S3 only.
Single dataset (CUAD, legal contracts domain). Generalization to healthcare, finance, and other S2/S3 domains untested.
Small sample size (N=48, 12 per task type). Confidence intervals are wide for entity-specific tasks.
Absence fingerprint attack not empirically evaluated. The vulnerability is characterized but mitigations are not tested.
ICL attack variant not evaluated. Session-level aggregation attacks not evaluated.
Local LLM (Phi-3) quality may bound synthesis step performance. Larger local models (Llama 70B) may yield different results.
Pipeline timing (31 minutes for 48 samples) not optimized; latency budget per query (~39 seconds) may be impractical for interactive use.
Summarize the four contributions: topic bottleneck mechanism, vocabulary exclusion hardening, local synthesis architecture, empirical operating envelope.
Headline numbers: 2.3% specific value recovery (vs. 91-94% for DP), 89.3% BERTScore F1 quality preservation.
Multi-domain evaluation beyond legal contracts (healthcare, finance, internal process).
Absence fingerprint mitigation testing: evaluate generation-time avoidance and random over-exclusion mitigations empirically.
ICL and session-level aggregation attacks. Larger local models (Llama 70B). Latency optimization.
Formal privacy guarantee connecting topic compression to information-theoretic bounds.
